title: Typewriter and Uniform
premise: In the autumn of a collapsing republic, Ivo Amberdale — a courier who has learned to measure the world in what fits in a satchel — is sent on the final diplomatic mission from a capital already falling to the army. When soldiers requisition the river town of Vellm and seize the municipal ledger containing the names of everyone marked for detention, Ivo and the town's aging archivist, Marta Quenn, must copy, hide, and smuggle the evidence past three checkpoints to the neutral consulate downriver. Betrayed by the very officer they hoped would help, Ivo discovers the mission's true purpose: the 'diplomatic pouch' they carry was always meant to be the ledger, and the republic intended them as decoys. In the end, Ivo burns their own courier's commission, passes the names to a stranger's hands, and survives not as an instrument of the state but as a witness — while Marta, who chose to stay behind with her typewriter and her records, becomes the memory the army could not requisition.
about_author: Noor Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated municipal records in post-war Europe. They write historical fiction about the small clerical acts — signatures, ledgers, requisition forms — through which great violence is administered.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Ivo Amberdale, POV. In the besieged capital, Ivo receives the last diplomatic commission: a sealed pouch, a rail warrant, and orders to reach the consulate at Greyharbor. The emotional beat is numb professionalism — Ivo measures the pouch, the rations, the lies, and refuses to think about what the republic's fall means for someone who has only ever been its hands.

chapters.title: Vellm on the River
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Stranded by a destroyed rail bridge, Ivo waits in the river town of Vellm and meets Marta Quenn, the municipal archivist, who is typing copies of every record in town 'before someone else decides what the record is.' The beat is wary warmth: two keepers of documents recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. At dawn the army occupies Vellm. Soldiers seal the town hall and confiscate the ledger of names — the list of dissidents, debtors, and foreign-born residents compiled by the old government, now a detention roster in new hands. Marta watches her life's work carried out in a gunnysack. The beat is violation.

chapters.title: What the Pouch Contains
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Ordered to report to the occupation commandant, Ivo is told the diplomatic pouch will be 'verified' — and realizes the army wants its contents, not its delivery. Ivo lies smoothly for the first time in a career of honest errands. The beat is the vertigo of switching sides without admitting it.

chapters.title: The Copyist's Night
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Marta reveals she kept carbons of the ledger, hidden in the lining of her typewriter case. She and Ivo retype the names through the night by stove-light while patrols pass the shutters. The beat is quiet defiance — ink as resistance, each name an act of refusal.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Studying the river route, Ivo maps the three checkpoints between Vellm and the neutral consulate: the bridge at Ostrel, the mill lock at Karn, and the pontoon at Greyharbor itself. Each demands papers; Ivo's courier warrant covers only one person, one pouch. The beat is cold arithmetic — two travelers, one set of papers.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Remembered
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Captain Elsen, an occupation officer who was schooled in Vellm, approaches Marta privately: he can get the carbons through Karn if she vouches the list is 'incomplete.' Marta suspects he wants to edit history, not save it. The beat is temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Terms of Carriage
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Ivo and Marta argue in the archive cellar: Ivo wants to split the list and carry half alone; Marta refuses to let any name be separated from the others. Their bargain — they go together, the typewriter case between them, and if one is taken the other burns their half. The beat is trust as a calculated risk.

chapters.title: Ostrel Bridge
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. First checkpoint: the carbons pass sewn into a child's coat Marta carries, while Ivo's warrant and decoy pouch absorb the soldiers' attention. A sergeant recognizes the courier's seal and hesitates — Ivo talks past the moment of recognition. The beat is terror disguised as boredom.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Sold Bread
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. On the road, a baker's boy who saw them at the bridge asks for payment for his silence — then, hearing what the papers are, asks instead to have his father's name read aloud from the list, to know if he is on it. He is. The beat is grief arriving as information.

chapters.title: Karn Mill Lock
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Second checkpoint: Captain Elsen is waiting, offering passage through the lock in exchange for the 'complete' list — and for Ivo's confession that the pouch is a decoy. Ivo must choose between the mission and the man. The beat is a bargain that smells like a trap.

chapters.title: What Elsen Kept
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Elsen lets them through but keeps a page — the names of officers who signed the old government's detention orders, including his own father. Marta realizes he is not censoring the list; he is hiding inside it. The beat is the discovery that corruption wears many uniforms, including a sympathetic one.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. A night journey by barge with a smuggler who charges in secrets rather than coin. Ivo tells the smuggler nothing and pays with the courier's warrant instead — surrendering the last document that proves who they are. The beat is liberation disguised as loss.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. At a river inn, a radio announces the capital has fallen and the republic 'has ceased to exist' — meaning Ivo's commission, and the pouch's diplomatic immunity, died with it. The soldiers at Greyharbor will no longer be obliged to honor any papers. The beat is the ground dissolving under the plan.

chapters.title: Decoys, After All
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Ivo finally opens the official pouch: inside is not a treaty but a second list — of couriers, including Ivo's own name and description, marked expendable. The mission was always meant to draw the army's eyes while someone else carried the real evidence. The beat is betrayal by the dead state one still serves.

chapters.title: Greyharbor Pontoon
chapters.summary: Ivo and Marta, alternating. Third checkpoint: the pontoon at Greyharbor, where soldiers now search everyone. Ivo walks the line as a nameless traveler, Marta behind with the typewriter case, and the sergeant who hesitated at Ostrel is transferred to this post. The beat is fate closing in with bureaucratic courtesy.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Held for questioning, Marta is made to open the case. She begins, calmly, to read the names aloud — all of them — as testimony, forcing the sergeant to decide whether he is confiscating papers or silencing the dead and the condemned. The beat is memory weaponized; the typewriter becomes a witness stand.

chapters.title: Fire at the Pontoon
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. In the confusion, the barge smuggler returns and sets a diversionary fire on the pontoon's stores. Ivo grabs the carbons, but the decoy pouch — and with it Ivo's last tie to the republic — burns. The beat is climax: chaos, choice, and the deliberate destruction of one's old identity.

chapters.title: Neutral Ground
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Across the pontoon, in the consulate's lamplight, Ivo hands the complete list to a consular clerk and asks only that the names be entered into the record — not negotiated, not traded. The clerk hesitates; Ivo stands unmoving until the pages are stamped. The beat is the quiet triumph of the archive over the army.

chapters.title: The One Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Marta refuses exile. She returns upriver to occupied Vellm with her typewriter and an empty case, intending to keep a second ledger — this time of what the army does. Ivo cannot argue with a woman who has already outlasted two governments. The beat is farewell without tragedy: memory needs someone on the ground.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Months later, in a refugee hostel, Ivo carries nothing official at all — no warrant, no pouch, no seal. A letter arrives from Marta via the baker's boy's family: the second ledger survives, page by page, in a hundred strangers' memories. The beat is inheritance: the names now belong to everyone who carries them.

chapters.title: Typewriter and Uniform
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV, years after the war. At a hearing where the ledger's names are finally read into the historical record, Ivo watches a young archivist — trained by Marta, who lived to see the occupation end — feed carbons into a typewriter to make the official copy. The beat is resolution: power corrupts the uniform, but the typewriter, and those who serve it, outlast every regime.
